answer:
OCR/import issues are directly and causally linked to worse onboarding performance, and they also drive additional support effort.

**Onboarding delays:** OCR/import issues are a quantified onboarding blocker. Implementing teams identified "OCR Processing: Extracting readable text from poorly scanned legacy PDF manuals" as the cause of 25% of onboarding delays [NL-012#NL-012-S06], and "OCR and Scanned PDFs" as 25% of delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04]. Scanned, image-only PDFs cause failed ingestion and incomplete text extraction, adding weeks to the schedule; e.g., Northstar Financial's scanned policy repository delayed pilot kickoff by three weeks [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. BrightPath Healthcare had the longest onboarding at 9.5 weeks due to "OCR / Scanned PDF Compliance" issues [NL-012#NL-012-S06] and "manual formatting checks on scanned compliance files" [NL-031#NL-031-S04].

**Go-live failure (performance metric threshold):** Because the citation engine requires a text layer, image-only PDFs without OCR cause citation accuracy to drop and the tenant to "fail our go-live quality checks" [NL-015#NL-015-S04]. Scanned PDFs "return incomplete citations, failing our go-live validation threshold (which requires 85% citation correctness)" [NL-031#NL-031-S04].

**Remediation and support cost:** When OCR/import issues cause a tenant to fail the citation/groundedness thresholds during Phase 6, the implementation lead halts go-live and triggers a mandatory remediation path; if accuracy remains below threshold after retesting, the project escalates to the VP of Customer Success, and a steering committee may "allocate additional support hours" [NL-005#NL-005-S11]. This ties OCR-induced failures directly to extra support consumption.

**Import performance and queue clogging:** OCR/import issues also degrade the import pipeline itself. Dumping large batches of scanned PDFs into the same queue as text-rich uploads blocks fast uploads; the March 14 upload outage was an import worker retry storm, motivating a split-queue architecture (Fast Queue vs Batch/OCR Queue) with strict rate limits [NL-021#NL-021-S06]. OCR is also provisioned as a dedicated enterprise extension (Advanced OCR Ingestion Queue) for scanned heritage PDFs [NL-005#NL-005-S09].

**Ongoing support correlation:** Recurring blockers, including OCR/scanned PDFs, are "reviewed monthly against onboarding metrics and support ticket patterns" [NL-005#NL-005-S11], establishing a monitored correlation between onboarding blockers and support tickets.
